verdict.rationale: The two diffs are functionally identical. Each builds a normalized-email to index Map once, keeps the first occurrence when existing duplicates collide, and registers appended contacts so duplicates inside the incoming list still merge with each other. Both reports are accurate and say what was verified. A explicitly explains how incoming duplicates are handled. B checked equivalence on 200 random inputs with mixed casing and duplicates. Neither difference is enough to prefer one over the other.
a_issues: No regression test added for the first-match-wins behavior when the existing list has duplicate emails.
Equivalence was checked on only one synthetic benchmark dataset.
b_issues: No regression test added for the first-match-wins behavior when the existing list has duplicate emails.
The report does not explicitly mention that duplicates within the incoming list still merge, which is the subtle part of the change.

verdict.rationale: The two diffs are functionally identical. Each builds a Map from normalized email to index once, keeps the first occurrence, and registers appended contacts so that duplicates within the incoming list still merge. Both reports are accurate, and each was verified with tests, typecheck and a timing run. A ran a randomized equivalence check across edge cases, and B confirmed byte-identical output on the full-scale benchmark. That is not a meaningful difference, so I would be equally happy to merge either.
a_issues: No regression test added (e.g., for duplicates already in the existing list, or a scale/performance guard).
The benchmark and the equivalence harness were deleted, so the verification can't be reproduced.
b_issues: No regression test added (e.g., for duplicates already in the existing list, or a scale/performance guard).
The benchmark scripts were kept outside the repo, so the verification can't be reproduced from the PR.
